Bangladesh DHS 2017-18. A literacy test was administered to women aged 15-49 whose highest level of educational attendance was primary schooling or lower. The test consisted of an enumerator administered assessment on the ability of the respondent to read a short and simple sentence. Those who could partially or fully read the sentence are considered literate. Respondents above the educational attainment threshold for whom the test was not administered were imputed as literate.

Those who could partially or fully read the sentence are considered literate. Respondents above the educational attainment threshold for whom the test was not administered were imputed as literate.
Bangladesh DHS 2022. A literacy test was administered to women aged 15-49 whose highest level of educational attendance was upper secondary schooling or lower.

Bangladesh DHS 2017-18. A literacy test was administered to women aged 15-49 whose highest level of educational attendance was primary schooling or lower. The test consisted of an enumerator administered assessment on the ability of the respondent to read a short and simple sentence. Those who could partially or fully read the sentence are considered literate. Respondents above the educational attainment threshold for whom the test was not administered were imputed as literate. Literacy status was imputed via a statistical model for older age groups not covered by the assessment.

Bangladesh DHS 2017-18. A literacy test was administered to women aged 15-49 whose highest level of educational attendance was primary schooling or lower. The test consisted of an enumerator administered assessment on the ability of the respondent to read a short and simple sentence. Those who could partially or fully read the sentence are considered literate. Respondents above the educational attainment threshold for whom the test was not administered were imputed as literate. Literacy status was imputed via a statistical model for older age groups not covered by the assessment.
